expansion:
A is correct. Prolonged outpatient topical anesthetic use is unsafe because it impairs corneal surface repair: the lecture states that these drops “Inhibit epithelial healing,” “Cause stromal melting,” and can produce “Anaesthetic keratopathy → perforation”; therefore, they should “NEVER” be prescribed for prolonged outpatient use (L15,16, page 48). In a corneal abrasion, pain relief may encourage repeated use while the injured cornea continues to be damaged and loses protective sensation.

B is wrong. Acute angle-closure glaucoma results from obstruction of aqueous outflow at the anterior chamber angle, not from topical corneal anesthetic use (not taken from the course material).

C is wrong. Rapid cataract formation is not an adverse effect of topical tetracaine or other topical anesthetics (not taken from the course material).

D is wrong. Retinal detachment is separation of the retina and is not caused by prolonged topical anesthetic use (not taken from the course material).
objective: Prolonged topical anesthetic use inhibits corneal epithelial healing and can cause stromal melting, anesthetic keratopathy, and perforation.
